incident_report: Jumped only fairly.  Shortly after the start was bumped by ORIENTAL SURPRISE which shifted out.  J Orman stated that his instructions were to endeavour to shift to the outside in the Home Straight but was unable to do so.  He said when placed under pressure SUPERB GUY finished the race off in a one-paced manner and, in his opinion, may have reached the end of its preparation.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings. <2/7/2026 Additional Veterinary Report> SUPERB GUY, which performed disappointingly, was examined by the Veterinary Officer who said at that time there were no significant findings. SUPERB GUY was again examined by the Veterinary Officer at the stables of Trainer K W Lui this morning. He said at this time he noted the horse to be lame in its right front leg. Before being allowed to race again, SUPERB GUY will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

For some distance near the 300 Metres made contact with JOLLY JUMPER when endeavouring to obtain a run when there was not sufficient room between JOLLY JUMPER and MANYTHANKS FOREVER.  As a result SPEEDY TRIDENT was held up for clear running between the 400 Metres and the 200 Metres when unable to obtain the run.  K Teetan was advised to exercise more care.  Sent for sampling post-race. For some distance approaching the 300 Metres was hampered when bumped by SPEEDY TRIDENT which was endeavouring to shift out. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  Sent for sampling post-race.

On jumping made contact with FLOWING RICHES due to both runners shifting ground.  When questioned regarding his riding of GOLDEN ACE, which was having its first race start, E Brown stated that his instructions were to settle the horse where comfortable and he was given no other instructions in relation to where to position the horse during the event.  He said after being bumped at the start he did not ride his mount along in the early stages to allow it to balance and settle where comfortable in accordance with his instructions.  When questioned if there was an opportunity to encourage his mount to hold a more forward position Jockey Brown stated that as the horse raced greenly he elected to allow it to settle towards the rear of the field where it was travelling comfortably.  He added that throughout the middle stages GOLDEN ACE continued to race greenly and entering the course proper near the 400 Metres became unbalanced.  He said when positioned behind and to the outside of GOOD POWER near the 400 Metres he contemplated shifting to the inside of that runner to follow LAHORE but elected to remain racing behind JUICY DRAGON as he was of the opinion that horse was travelling well enough to provide him with a horse to follow into the event.  When questioned if there was an opportunity to ride the horse with more vigour between the 400 Metres and the 200 Metres Jockey Brown stated that as he was still assessing where he was going to improve he continued to encourage his mount forward but not applying full vigour which allowed GOLDEN ACE to improve behind JUICY DRAGON.  He said when JUICY DRAGON did not improve as he had expected this resulted in GOLDEN ACE being badly held up for clear running behind JUICY DRAGON between the 200 Metres and the 150 Metres before he was able to shift to that runner’s outside to secure clear running.  He further stated that from this point on GOLDEN ACE finished the race off well under hard riding.  Trainer C Fownes confirmed the instructions issued and expressed satisfaction with Jockey Brown’s ride.  After considering his explanation the Stewards advised Jockey Brown that, in their opinion, he should have applied more pressure to the horse in the early stages to maintain a more forward position and secondly between the 400 Metres and the 200 Metres to ride his mount with more urgency to endeavour to improve to the inside of JUICY DRAGON earlier in the Home Straight.  Jockey Brown was advised that in future he should ride his mounts in a manner to leave no room for query.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings. Approaching the 250 Metres became unbalanced when crowded between BETTER AND BETTER and LAHORE which shifted out slightly.
